title: Council approves 2025 Region of Waterloo budget
subtitle: Police and library budgets, transit fare changes, a 5% cap on some expenses, and the new fees by-law.
overview: Regional Council approved the 2025 Region of Waterloo plan and budget {{vote:m1}}. The operating budget has a net expenditure of $1,684,964,914 and a property tax levy of $831,778,942. The same motion approved the Waterloo Regional Police Service and Region of Waterloo Libraries budgets, along with the capital budget and 2026-2034 forecast.

The budget also includes changes to Grand River Transit. Children aged 6 and under will ride at the child fare, with the change planned for July 2025. A pilot will subsidize EasyGO 2-Fare cards for not-for-profit agencies. Council also capped the increase in several expense categories at 5%, and the 2025 budget was reduced by $6,938,000 as a result. Staff are to find those savings, and council discussed asking for a report on where they come from. A new Fees and Charges by-law was also passed.

For residents, the budget sets the 2025 regional property tax levy and confirms service funding that starts January 1. Staff told council that deferring the budget would delay some planned spending, including expanded warming centres. A motion to defer the budget to January was defeated.

decisions.detail: Council approved the 2025 Plan and Operating Budget, with a net expenditure of $1,684,964,914 and a property tax levy of $831,778,942, plus the capital budget and 2026-2034 forecast.

Council capped the increase in supplies, equipment, facilities maintenance, professional fees, communications, travel and facility occupancy at 5%, reducing the 2025 operating budget by $6,938,000 overall.
Council approved the Waterloo Regional Police Service 2025 operating budget, with a net expenditure of $278,467,629 and a levy of $252,468,301, and its capital budget and forecast.
Council approved the 2025 Region of Waterloo Libraries operating budget, with a net property tax levy of $3,182,053, and its capital budget and forecast.
GRT staff are to update the fees by-law so the child fare covers children 6 and under, effective July 2025, and report back on revenue impacts through the 2025-2030 Business Plan.
Council allocated $25,000 in deferred fare revenue to a pilot that lets eligible not-for-profit agencies buy up to 500 EasyGO 2-Fare cards a year at $3 instead of $5.
Council delayed the Walker Road project in the 2025 capital budget and cut the one-time contribution to the transportation capital reserve by $465,000.
Council passed By-law 24-052, which sets new and adjusted fees and charges for 2025 and repeals the earlier fees by-law.

debate: Some councillors said the 5% cap handed budget decisions to staff, so council would not decide where the roughly $6.9 million in cuts fell. Others said staff are only working within a cap council set, and that nothing is being struck from services.

Councillors argued over a report back on the cuts. Some wanted council approval of the cuts. Others said that would reopen the budget and stop it passing that day, so the report would be for information.

Staff said only part of each dollar of gross spending falls on the tax levy because other governments and user rates cover the rest. The effect of the cap on the levy was therefore much smaller than the headline cut.

Supporters of a deferral to January wanted a lower tax increase. Opponents said staff could not rework the budget in six weeks and that delay would hold up services such as expanded warming centres and food bank funding.

Several councillors said the Region pays for services that belong to the province and federal government, and called for a new funding deal for municipalities. One councillor voting against said the increase was too high for residents under financial strain.
